## Design

### 2026-10-10 – 11/10/26

**4.9h**

11/10/26
Finally completed schematic.

Learnt some intrusting new stuff today like the data buses such as SPI (how you can share multiple devices on it and the restrictions of doing that etc...) or UART and how RX is IN and TX is OUT, nice practise for the drone / rocket as they use a variety of data busses for their sensors.

Selected the STM32G431CBT6 because it was available in LQFP- 48, has a FPU, CRC and mathematical accelerator  which is what I need for an IMU, most importantly it has an internal clock allowing me to save costs on ordering an external clock and its load capacitors.

Originally I was going to go with a USB connection for programming via DFU as well but than I found out SWDIO can do VERY important things DFU can not like setting a breakpoint to debug values from sensor which in the future I would definitely need to write firmware for the IMU. So I thought, might as well just remove the ESD protection IC for the D+ / D- lines and save money.

Chosen the LSM6DS3TR-C because its a 6 axis +/- 2000dps +/16g  IMU for a very good price, and I can solve the degree of error in firmware.

Since the MCU has so many free pins it would be a waste to not use them all so i decided to use headers and turn it into a full dev-board with a built in IMU, that way I can test out other sensors I'm planning to use in preparation for designing a flight computer for a drone or rocket.

To speed up development I borrowed some pieces of my USB-C hub schematic such as  the LDO and USB-C port that I'm using for power, also I'm going to be truthful I used ai to summarise the datasheets and connections other wise I'm going to spend so much time scrolling through endless pages of info that you mostly not need / laid in a very annoying format such as the pin functions, very annoying to go through rows and rows of columns that aren't even related to the package you are using... TT  (I hope this is allowed )..... I did learn most of the stuff about PCBs design from research I did for my USB-C hub. (https://stardance.hackclub.com/projects/40392)

So did a 4 stack PCB 1st layer for signals. 2and layer for GND 3rd layer for 3V3 and 4th for 3V3 stitching and signals. I recorded notes in my notebook so ill do the rest of the dev log later...

UPDATE:
faaaahhh just realised i need to get this done cause submission is in 1 hour.

For component placement I split the board into 3 parts, IMU, MCU and USB-C with LDO and I placed their required components such as decoupling / filtering capacitors, before organizing those groups on the board.

Since I wanted a small compact board I limited the board side to around a 4cm square, but that caused the issue of not having any space for the m3 screws and since m3 screws are only what i have lying around I had to add the m3 screw holes in a x shape pattern with filleted corners for strength.

I had to route signals on the 3V3 plane on L3 so that lead to the 3v3 plane being torn apart so i had to create another fill on L4 the signal routing layer to stitch the 3V3 plane with vias.

Man if there hadn't been DRC I would have been cooked.... Like so many unconnected 3V3s and GNDS, crazy, always check DRC guys lmao.

So I routed SCK traces away from sensitive traces like INT 1 /2 as noise from SCK might interfere with INT1 /2 which tell the MCU when its ready to take new data, if falsely triggered it would give duplicate values, which would be pain to debug...

Thanks for reading, now im going to sleep, i have school tmr :skull:
